title: Update on Singapore's COVID-19 Vaccination Programme
what_it_is: Update on Singapore's COVID-19 Vaccination Programme

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination programme questions
sections.summary: Questions were asked on vaccination proportions, rejected appointments, essential workers, programme updates and antibody measurement, with free vaccination and expanded centres stated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) to date, what proportion of persons aged (i) over-70 years (ii) 60 to 70 years and (iii) under 60 years have taken the COVID-19 vaccine; and (b) what measures are in place to increase the voluntary take-up of the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the proportion of persons invited to make COVID-19 vaccination appointments who have been rejected due to them failing the pre-vaccination questionnaire; and (b) how is the Ministry adjusting its vaccination plans to minimise wastage of vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the number of workers in the essential services sector who have gone through the COVID-19 vaccination; and (b) what are the criteria for the selection of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether he can provide an update on the COVID-19 vaccination programme; and (b) whether the Ministry intends to measure the antibody levels of persons (either as a class or individually) over time after they have been vaccinated to assess whether these persons retain immunity against the COVID-19 virus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Vaccination is free for all Singaporeans and long-term residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have expanded the number of vaccination centres to 31 today and there will be a total of 40 vaccination centres islandwide by mid-April, so that individuals can be conveniently vaccinated near their home or place of work.

sections.label: Vaccine doses administered
sections.summary: As of 3 April 2021, around 1.52 million doses were administered, with 1.05 million receiving at least one dose and over 468,000 completing full vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As of 3 April 2021, around 1.52 million COVID-19 vaccine doses have been administered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Around 1.05 million individuals have received at least one dose of the vaccine, of which more than 468,000 individuals have received their second dose and completed the full vaccination regimen.

sections.label: Eligible individuals vaccination booking
sections.summary: About 17% of eligible individuals have been vaccinated or booked appointments, with the rest expected to receive SMS by mid-May and slots by early June.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To date, about 17% of eligible individuals have received the vaccination or booked their appointments and we expect the rest should receive the SMS by the middle of May and they can expect a booking slot by early June.

sections.label: Monitoring vaccine immunity
sections.summary: MOH will study immunity duration by collecting post-vaccination samples from groups like healthcare workers and seniors, with no plans to test everyone's serology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MOH will be conducting further studies to monitor and review the extent and duration of immunity provided by the COVID-19 vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This includes collecting selected post-vaccination samples from groups such as healthcare workers, frontline staff and seniors, to monitor the persistence of antibodies up to 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Currently, in line with international practices, there are no plans to test the serology of everyone who is vaccinated in Singapore.

sections.label: Expanding vaccination programme
sections.summary: As more vaccine stocks arrive, the programme will expand so all Singaporeans and long-term residents can be vaccinated by end-2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: As more vaccine stocks arrive, we will continue to expand our vaccination programme to more segments of the population, so that all Singaporeans and long-term residents in Singapore will have the chance to be vaccinated by end-2021.

sections.label: Ramadan mosque staff risk
sections.summary: A question was asked whether mosque staff and volunteers at Ramadan night prayers are at increased infection risk, with continued study of prioritisation challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Would mosque staff and volunteers involved in additional night prayers during the holy month of Ramadan be considered to be at increased risk of infection, given that they are expected to serve at least 250 congregants a day?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will continue to study how best to deal with the challenges of prioritising those most at risk, those who have some urgent need and having some equitable distribution across our population, even as we try to cover as many people as possible before the end of the year.

sections.label: Shift in advice
sections.summary: Ms Lim is correct that the advice has shifted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ms Lim is correct; indeed, the advice has shifted.

sections.label: Antibody assays and variants
sections.summary: Assaying antibodies from prior vaccination may not inform clinical risk for a new variant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we need to be sure that it is useful and necessary before we would do such a thing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: However, with the issue of variants, assaying a set of antibodies to a prior vaccination is not going to be necessarily useful to inform the clinical risk for a new variant that perhaps was not there when the vaccination was delivered.

sections.label: Vaccination for overseas travel
sections.summary: Travellers need vaccination as they will not benefit from Singapore's herd immunity overseas; vaccinations hoped for all eligible by end 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But you can also imagine that we would perhaps want to make sure that individuals who want to travel overseas would also continue to be protected and that requires them to be vaccinated because, once they are overseas, they will not benefit from herd immunity here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, let us get that number as high as possible and we hope to be able to offer the vaccinations to all eligible Singaporeans along with residents by the end of 2021.

sections.label: Tracking essential workers' vaccinations
sections.summary: Essential workers are not given priority, and vaccination completion is tracked through employers and regulatory bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After that, all are not being given priority to go for their vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are, indeed, tracking the completion of vaccinations among the essential workers closely and we do so through the employers as well as some of the regulatory bodies for the relevant domain.

sections.label: Vaccine supply limit
sections.summary: The issue is the limit of vaccine supplies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The issue is the limit of our vaccine supplies.
